name: Qualcomm
description: Qualcomm earns money two ways. QCT sells Snapdragon and related chip platforms (processors, modems, RF and connectivity) for phones, cars and IoT devices: 87 percent of FY2025 revenue at a 30 percent pre-tax margin. QTL licenses its cellular patents to phone makers for a royalty on each device: 13 percent of revenue but about 25 percent of segment pre-tax profit at a 72 percent margin. Phones are 63 percent of total revenue, so it is exposed to a few customers (Apple, Samsung and Xiaomi were each 10 percent or more), and Apple has started using its own modem instead of Qualcomm's. Handset chip revenue fell 19.6 percent year on year in the June 2026 quarter while automotive rose 61 percent.

gics.note: Conventional GICS label as shown on Wikipedia's List of S&P 500 companies (columns GICS Sector and GICS Sub-Industry). That page does not show the industry group or industry, so those are null rather than filled from memory.

hq.note: 5775 Morehouse Dr., San Diego (FY2025 10-K cover); incorporated in California 1985, reincorporated in Delaware 1991

employees.note: About 52,000 full-time, part-time and temporary workers, the overwhelming majority full-time employees, in 38 countries (FY2025 10-K)

businessLines.name: QCT: Handsets
businessLines.how: Chip platforms sold per unit to phone makers; revenue is chipset volume times average selling price, with premium-tier Android platforms carrying higher prices.
businessLines.description: Snapdragon chip platforms (processors, modems, RF front-end, connectivity) for mobile handsets.

businessLines.name: QCT: Automotive
businessLines.how: Chip platforms sold per unit to car makers and Tier 1s for vehicle programs; revenue ramps with new vehicle launches.
businessLines.description: Snapdragon Digital Chassis: connectivity, digital cockpit, ADAS/automated driving platforms.

businessLines.name: QCT: IoT
businessLines.how: Chip platforms sold per unit into consumer, industrial and networking products.
businessLines.description: Consumer electronics, industrial devices and edge networking chips (Snapdragon and Dragonwing).

businessLines.name: QCT total
businessLines.description: Sum of the three streams above.

businessLines.name: QTL (Qualcomm Technology Licensing)
businessLines.how: Per-unit royalties, generally a percentage of the wholesale selling price charged by the licensee of each complete licensed product net of permitted deductions (10-K), under licence agreements of a set term; new long-term licences were signed in FY2025 with two key Chinese OEMs and with Transsion.
businessLines.description: Licences to Qualcomm's 3G/4G/5G and other patents to handset and device makers.

businessLines.name: QSI (Qualcomm Strategic Initiatives)
businessLines.how: No operating revenue (FY2025 $0; FY2024 $18M); earnings are gains and losses on marketable and non-marketable equity investments.

brands.name: Snapdragon
brands.share: Platform brand across handsets, automotive and IoT; revenue not split by brand
